**Status: detailed implementation plan.** The target names below are proposed
contracts, not declarations in the current graph. This page plans
[`4A_clean_clinic_diagnosis.R`][legacy-4a]; the execution plan absorbs
[`4B_clean_clinic_diagnosis.slurm`][legacy-4b]. No scientific pipeline is run
or newly wired by this plan.

The result is a harmonized measurement table for each dictionary output group,
a separate record of the legacy rejected overlaps, and one reporting tracker.
Large intermediates stay in DuckDB-backed Parquet file targets. Small rules
and schemas stay in ordinary targets. Each procedure will become a short
declaration plus a separately explained transformation helper.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm Identities, Definitions, And Resource Boundaries"}

Require the completed clinic identity product from [page 20](20_page-construct-clinic-ids.qmd),
the dictionary and recorded `X` schema from [page 21](21_page-construct-diagnosis-dictionary.qmd),
and the prepared Wave 3 file from [page 18](18_page-prep-w3.qmd). The dictionary
schema checks must pass before interpreting any expression.

| Existing dependency | Role here |
| --- | --- |
| `s2_clinic_months_raw_zip`, `s2_clinic_months_members_chr` | Tracked source archive and ordered monthly member selectors |
| `s2_clinic_ids_df` | Six-field clinic-month identity join and longitudinal ID |
| `s3_diagnosis_dictionary_df` | Harmonized variables, per-wave expressions, and `filename` groups |
| `s3_w3_column_dictionary_df` | Authoritative description-to-`X` mapping |
| `s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet` | Prepared Wave 3 measurements, without collection into R |

Inventory the AVC, replacement diarrhea/pneumonia, and 2020 anemia members by
exact source suffix. Reuse page 21's archive selectors where already defined.
Record schemas, encodings, periods, and row-order provenance before migration.
Do not read an old scratch dictionary or independently recreate its `X` names.

Before running later implementations, select a worker count and per-worker
budget within one approved allocation. The [execution page](../releases/20_page-execute-pipeline.qmd#parallel-targets-execution-plan)
owns that configuration; this page will contain no `future::plan()`, nested
worker pool, standalone Slurm launcher, or global object-size override.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Prepare The Dictionary Evaluation Rules"}

Build `s4a_diagnosis_wave12_expected_columns_df` by splitting the Wave 1/2
expressions into distinct source terms. Build
`s4a_diagnosis_evaluation_rules_df` from the same dictionary, retaining wave,
`var`, source terms, and output group. Validate the supported expression
grammar before compiling it to DuckDB operations; do not evaluate arbitrary
text from a source file as unrestricted R code.

Preserve the distinction between direct terms and sums:

| Expression | Legacy treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Single earlier-wave term | Return the term, including its original missing-value sentinel behavior |
| Sum of earlier-wave terms | Replace `-1` components with zero before addition |
| Single Wave 3 term | Preserve the term's missing value |
| Sum of Wave 3 terms | Replace missing components with zero before addition |

Keep absent expected columns distinct from explicit zero reports. Do not
convert all negative values or missing values to zero. Record the handling of
an entirely unavailable expression and test it against the legacy result.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage Supplements And Decode One Monthly Member"}

Write `s4a_diagnosis_wave12_supplements_parquet` from AVC and the corrected
diarrhea/pneumonia input. Retain all measurement rows and normalize the latter's
`Variable` using its `cCode` and final underscore suffix. The distinct schema
table from page 21 is not a substitute for these measurements.

Declare one `s4a_diagnosis_wave12_month_inputs_parquet` branch per selected
monthly member. Extract privately, decode with verified source settings, drop
the superseded `fname == 1` codes `DySS`, `DiSS`, `DiDy`, `P`, and `PGRA`, then
append supplements for that member's year and month. Keep source provenance.

Illustrative future wiring, using the existing ordinary member-name vector:

```r
# Proposed declaration; not tangled or included in _targets.R yet.
tar_target(
  s4a_diagnosis_wave12_month_inputs_parquet,
  s4a_diagnosis_write_month_input_fn(
    s2_clinic_months_raw_zip,
    s2_clinic_months_members_chr,
    s4a_diagnosis_wave12_supplements_parquet
  ),
  pattern = map(s2_clinic_months_members_chr),
  format = "file"
)
```

The helper will write a branch-unique destination and return its path. Later
per-file branches may map over this file target because it has a pattern.
A static file bundle must not become a per-file branch dimension.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Join Clinic Identities And Apply The Reporting Filter"}

Join on `cAnnee`, `cPeriode`, `cCodeNiv`, `cCodeStru`, `cNom`, and `fname`, with
the legacy character conversions for codes. Reproduce the actual
`month_df[clinicID, on = ...]` join direction and multiplicity in fixtures;
do not silently substitute an inner join or a conventional left join without
checking unmatched rows and inventory multiplicity.

Exclude `qCHtCHkwqtQ`, including the source filter's removal of missing IDs,
and apply the three literal variable-name repairs (`c$_`, `_*`, and
`SOMME ACCTS`). Retain
clinic/year/month/file groups only when `sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE) > 0`.
That is the earlier-wave rule; it differs from Wave 3's count of positive
measurements. A group containing both positive and negative values can expose
the difference, so it needs a dedicated fixture.

Keep these transformations in the monthly disk-backed relation, owned by the
next reduced checkpoint, rather than returning the tall table to the manager.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Classify And Reduce Earlier-Wave Duplicates"}

Compute flags per clinic/year/month/file/`Variable`: multiple distinct values,
multiple distinct nonmissing numeric values, and duplicate row count. Choose
the reduction at the wider clinic/year/month/file/`cCode` level, in the source's
ordered precedence:

| Decision | Condition and reduction |
| --- | --- |
| `unique` | No variable has differing values; retain the unique value |
| `unique_nonNA` | No numeric disagreement; retain the unique nonmissing value, or missing if all are missing |
| `sum` | Numeric disagreement exists and all variable flags indicate differences; sum with missing values omitted |
| `sum2` | Numeric disagreement exists and every duplicated variable differs; use the same sum |
| `error` | None of the preceding rules applies; retain the legacy `-99` conflict sentinel |

Persist `s4a_diagnosis_wave12_deduplicated_parquet` and an aggregate decision
audit. The helper `s4a_diagnosis_drop_na_if_fn` must preserve empty-input and
multiple-value behavior. Do not reuse page 18's maximum reduction: these are
different scientific operations.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Map The Earlier-Wave Measurements In Bounded Units"}

For each month, evaluate `fname == 1` and `fname > 1` against their respective
dictionary columns. Retain the `-1` encoding and add absent expected source
columns with the correct missing semantics before evaluation. Write
`s4a_diagnosis_wave12_month_mapped_parquet` with IDs, period, `fname`, and
harmonized `V` columns. The manager receives paths, not a `list_rbind()` of
all months.

Prototype a month-wide disk-backed result first. If mapping width still
exceeds the worker budget, subdivide evaluation by dictionary output group
after the reporting and duplicate decisions have been made. Keep a common
report universe so a report with only missing mapped values is not lost.
Benchmark both layouts before fixing the branch count or adding another cache.

The old code skips a wave subset when its tall row count is at most one.
Record this edge case and obtain an explicit parity/correction decision;
do not turn the skipped case into accepted data as an incidental pivot change.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Insert The 2020 Anemia Data And Clean Wave 3"}

Read the actual anemia measurements into
`s4a_diagnosis_wave3_anemia_parquet`; page 21's anemia schema target contains
only names. Preserve the question-mark header repair and metadata exclusions.
For 2020, remove the old anemia fields and reproduce the original full join
on the shared organisation/period keys. Retain non-2020 rows and the recorded
column order in `s4a_diagnosis_wave3_anemia_corrected_parquet`.

Use the page-21 schema to assign `X` names while preserving identifier fields.
Remove `V1`, `TYPE`, `FS`, and `code_fs` before exact-row deduplication. Resolve
`X1067`, `X1068`, and `X1736` through that schema, record the corresponding
descriptions, and convert their negative values to missing. The checkpoint is
`s4a_diagnosis_wave3_deduplicated_parquet`.

For `s4a_diagnosis_wave3_reporting_parquet`, retain rows with at least one
positive measurement, excluding the refrigerator-temperature fields `X1708`
and `X1709`. Use 3A expressions for 2020 and 3B for later periods, assign
`fname = 6`, and write `s4a_diagnosis_wave3_mapped_parquet`. Partition by complete
periods only after operations requiring the full duplicate group are safe.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Resolve Report Sources And Write The Tracker"}

Create `s4a_clinic_reporting_candidates_parquet` from mapped report keys
before projecting output variables. Implement one tested source-selection helper shared by the tracker
and diagnosis outputs.

| Period | Expected `fname` |
| --- | --- |
| Before 2015; January–March 2015 | 1 |
| April–December 2015; 2016 | 2 |
| 2017 / 2018 / 2019 | 3 / 4 / 5 |
| 2020 onward | 6 |
| Otherwise | 0 |

Prefer the expected file when present; otherwise retain candidates at the
minimum absolute file-number distance. The source retains distance ties.
Expose them in `s4a_report_selection_audit_df`; do not silently choose a first
row. A scalar wide reporting tracker needs an agreed resolution of any ties
that would create list-valued cells.

Write `s4a_clinic_reporting_track_parquet` at
`data/intermediates/clinic_reporting_track.parquet`, with one clinic row,
`yYYYY_mMM` columns, and zero for no retained report in the defined calendar.
This is the single handoff to metadata assembly; there is no separate
clean-to-intermediate copy step.

Record the legacy set of emitted calendar columns. Expanding it to include
periods with no reports anywhere is a separate schema decision, not an
incidental effect of completing a date sequence.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Partition Retained And Rejected Diagnosis Outputs"}

Derive the ordinary character branch driver `s4a_diagnosis_output_groups_chr`
from the dictionary's actual `filename` values. Each branch reads only its
`V` columns from mapped Parquet artifacts, resolves `fname` with the shared
helper, and writes tracked retained and legacy `wrong_fname` Parquet files
under `data/intermediates/by_diagnosis/`. Keep `fname` in the outputs.

`s4a_diagnosis_output_parquet` may return a two-path bundle per output-group
branch. Treat that bundle as one branch unit; any later per-file iteration
needs its own ordinary path selector and dynamic file-tracking target.

The legacy `wrong_fname` predicate records wrong files only when an expected
file exists. It does not record all non-nearest fallback candidates when no
expected file exists. Preserve that meaning and report the uncovered
selection category separately in the audit; changing the rejected-output
definition requires an explicit decision.

Parallelism comes from the graph's ready monthly, period, and output-group
branches, dispatched by the controller configured for `tar_make()`. A branch
does not launch its own futures or submit another Slurm job.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Specify Stage 4 Acceptance Evidence"}

This block defines tests to implement, not claims that stage 4 has run.

| Verification layer | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Synthetic logic tests | Exact duplicates, mixed missing/numeric values, all-missing groups, `sum`/`sum2`, and `-99` conflicts; identity join direction; direct-term versus summed-term missing semantics |
| Boundary fixtures | One-row wave subsets; March/April 2015; 2019/2020; exact source present, nearest fallback, and equal-distance ties; empty output partitions |
| Wave 3 fixtures | Anemia-only full-join rows; schema order changes; the three negative repairs; refrigerator fields excluded only from the reporting decision |
| Parquet round trip | Schema, column order, UTF-8, missing values, sentinels, and exact retained keys |
| Reference comparison | Canonically keyed values against the legacy result, with reviewed differences recorded rather than normalized away |
| Post-build summaries | Rows and clinics by period/wave/output group; duplicate decisions; missing IDs; source-choice categories; tracker/output agreement |
| Resource verification | Peak memory and elapsed time per branch; scalar SQL row counts and file sizes without collecting full data; serial/parallel equality and a no-op second build |

Create `tests/check-clinic-diagnosis.R` with synthetic fixtures before wiring
the stage. Run graph/branchability checks before any separately authorized
data build. Historical comments such as 122,924 retained Wave 3 rows are
comparison points, not unconditional assertions for changed inputs.

The plan's structure can be checked now:

```sh
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```
